audience.programmeDescription: Leiden History studies political, social, economic and cultural change from antiquity to the present, with attention to Europe and its connections with the world. Source criticism, historical research and written and oral argument are central. The revised first two years include digital humanities and a sequence of research seminars.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The displayed 150 EC comprises 120 EC of historical study and illustrated second-year choices, plus 30 EC of elective or minor space. The remaining 30 required EC, including the exact final research allocation and progression rules for the revised curriculum, still need confirmation. A complete comparison with UCR remains unfinished; no UCR alternative is shown here.

curriculum.limitation: Verified subset: 150 of 180 EC. This includes 60 EC of required first-year study, 60 EC of second-year required study and restricted choices, and 30 EC of elective space. The illustrated choices reflect the current annual menu and do not guarantee future offerings. Formal routes do not apply to entrants from 2025 onward. The remaining 30 required EC and their programme-specific final research and progression rules await confirmation. Both first-year research seminars must be passed before second-year research seminars; the usual study-advice threshold is 45 EC with at least one first-year research seminar passed. Individual course conditions also apply. Electives must meet level, approval and non-overlap rules.

componentNotes.y2-5532vpsy: Restricted 5 EC sources-and-methods choice. Entry requires Ancient History and the study-advice norm. Assessment includes assignments, a final paper and an oral presentation.
componentNotes.y2-5772ibm02y: Restricted 5 EC sources-and-methods choice, open to BA History students. Weekly assignments and a take-home examination each contribute half the grade.
componentNotes.y2-5732v013y: Restricted 10 EC autumn research seminar. The study-advice norm and both first-year research seminars must be passed; assessment includes a substantial research paper, participation and individual/group presentations.
componentNotes.y2-5772iaw62y: Restricted 10 EC spring research seminar. The study-advice norm and both first-year research seminars must be passed. The paper must pass; presentations, group work and participation also contribute.
componentNotes.open-elective-space: 30 EC for appropriate-level elective study or a minor. Examination-board approval is required except for recognised 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus. Courses must not overlap with required study, and Honours courses cannot count. History also excludes overlapping American History and Medieval/Early Modern History minor tracks. No particular elective subjects or semester split are assumed.
